In this case, you can check what type of low frequency noise exists by simple operation of this app.

In general, the low frequency sound is a sound wave with 1 Hz to 100 Hz. By depending on its frequency component and sound level, it is different the degree of influence on the human body and the noise sensation.

The measurement analysis is performed in the following step. Be sure to set the measurement conditions in Step-1 once before starting the sound measurement.

1) Calibration (Calibrate): A reference signal (1kHz sine wave) is output to determine the reference noise level for the low frequency component. If the volume level of iPhone is set to about 20-50%, the calibration will automatically adjust it to the optimum volume level for the reference signal.

2) Measurement (Measure) : Analyze a power level of low frequency sound. 
- LF Level (dB): Low frequency power level less than 100Hz. 
- Leq (dB): Sound power level with the frequency weight characteristic Z (Flat) of the audible band.

3) Measurement display: It can select either 1/3 octave band frequency analysis, FFT analysis or Time course graph. They are updated in real time.

And if you're just too wired to sleep, turn on the sweep second hand with a tap on the sweep button. It will make two full revolutions and then slowly fade out. You might find that as it fades, so do you to restful sleep.

ProjectR is an app for discovering and controlling PJLINK-enabled projectors via WiFi.

PJLINK is a TCP protocol for communicating with projectors (http://pjlink.jbmia.or.jp/english/). This app is a PJLINK client, giving you the ability to use your iPhone as a remote to control projectors which are PJLINK-enabled. (Most WiFi-enabled projectors made today support PJLINK.) The app also has the following features:

- Manually add a projector by its IP address
- Scan your WiFi network for PJLINK-enabled projectors
- Turn a projector on or off
- Change the projector input
- Mute the audio or video of a projector
- View status information about a projector like how many hours the bulb has been used, or any errors the projector is emitting.
- Operate on multiple projectors at once
